subject: Potential truncation error: missing data points?

messages.author: fc98df0ed215166f
messages.subject: Potential truncation error: missing data points?
parts:
Hello all,

I am working with line transect data collected from wild long-tailed macaques from 2 different strata.

1) The data set I am having a problem with is composed of 35 observations (23 in stratum 1 and 12 in stratum 2). I have selected 10% right truncation and manually pooled the data into 5 intervals. However, when I run the analysis, my observations are reduced to 18 and 10, respectively. A total of 7 observations have been omitted. Is there something I might have done unknowingly to further right truncate the data? The left truncation is set to 0 and I can't figure out how 10% truncation resulted in omitting 7/35 observations. 


2) I also had one more question about survey effort. The value generated by Distance for one of the strata seems abnormally low.
The total distance walked for each grid was:

B1 - 79.2 km
B2 - 68.2 km
 
Each grid had a strip width of 39m. The effort, however, was:

B1 - 5200
B2 - 9700

Is it normal for the effort to contradict the distance walked per transect? I would have expected the effort to be higher in B1 since we walked an extra 10+ km over the course of the year.

Thank you all for your help. I have tried to find faculty at my institution that are familiar with Distance to no avail. I'm very grateful for this group.

Best,
Lauren

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Potential truncation error: missing data points?
parts:
Lauren

You are below a reasonable number of samples for fitting your detection functions with the original 35 detections.  Moving on from that, I suspect the reason that exactly 3 or 4 detections (~10% of 35) is because having converted your exact distances to binned distances as a result of your 'manual pooling', the 10% most distant detections lies inside perhaps your final bin.  The entire bin will be excluded as a result of the truncation.  With 35 sightings it will be easy to check whether that is the case.  With larger sample sizes, and no binning, the percentage of sightings removed because of truncation may not be exactly 10% because of multiple sightings at the same distance.  But your small sample size and manual binning will exaggerate that effect.

As for your second question about effort, I need more information.  I understand that you say you walked the two distances in km.  I don't know where in the Distance output you plucked the second set of numbers, nor the units in which those numbers are expressed.  Perhaps you could provide more detailed program output.  How many transects per stratum, the length of each transect, perhaps the number of repeat walks of the transects?

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Potential truncation error: missing data points?
parts:
Hi Eric,

Thanks for your reply. I played around with the data a bit and realized that the effort value I was looking at was the combined length of all of the transects in the stratum (see the '4000.00' value in the attached image).

I now have another issue, unfortunately. I have run multiple analyses on both data sets using different key functions and adjustments. I have also spent a fair amount of time manually pooling the data in order to find the best fit (and I addressed the previous problem of truncation eliminating the last interval). I have double and triple checked that all of the units are correct, and yet the outputs that I am getting for group density and individual density are unreasonably high (e.g. 57 groups/square km instead of ~2).

I have attached an subset of the data. This particular data set contains 8 transects (1km each) with 153 surveys and 77 observations in total.

Does anything stand out as problematic?

Thank you again for your time.

Lauren
